title: Greens call for temporary ban on new data centres
summary:
Zack Polanski has called for a freeze on the approval of new data centres in England because of concerns about the amount of water and energy they use.
Data centres can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, although there are no official figures on how much water they consume in the UK.
The government said a pause would lead to the UK losing investment and being dependent on overseas computing for sensitive data processing.
There are hundreds of data centres in the UK – with plans for many more.
The amount of water data centres consume can change based on size, design and local climate - the hotter the area the more water needed to cool the equipment.

title: EPA Issues Permitting Guidance to Further President Trump’s Agenda Promoting Data Centers and Safeguarding Communities
summary:
EPA Issues Permitting Guidance to Further President Trump’s Agenda Promoting Data Centers and Safeguarding CommunitiesJuly 27, 2026Contact Information EPA Press Office ( press@epa.govWASHINGTON – This month, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) issued guidance clarifying that the Clean Air Act (CAA) Acid Rain Program (ARP) does not apply to power generation facilities that are not connected to a public electricity grid, commonly referred to as “islanded” power generation facilities.
The guidance expands opportunities for companies to develop and operate islanded power generation facilities for data centers.
This will give developers greater flexibility in where and how quickly they can build new facilities while helping to protect the environment and reducing burdens on communities’ electric grid.
This guidance furthers the principals of President Donald Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, which was expanded last week during an event at EPA.
EPA is proud to further the President’s agenda through commonsense approaches to regulating.”

title: Watch: What caused the flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet border
summary:
The US Geological Survey says the floods in the Nepal-Tibet border were triggered by a "glacial collapse" - meaning a glacier or part of a glacier had disintegrated.
Initial reports led authorities to believe that an earthquake had been the cause.
The cause of the glacial collapse has not been determined, but scientists have warned that Himalayan glaciers are melting at an accelerating rate due to rising temperatures and climate change.

title: Climate change is supercharging El Niños, coral records show
summary:
We’re in the midst of a blockbuster El Niño that could be become the strongest in living memory.
It and other very strong, recent El Niños are much stronger than those in the past as the result of human-caused climate change, a new study in Science shows.
Climate models have given mixed signals about whether El Niño events could become stronger with climate change.
Physical evidence from fossilized corals in the western and central Pacific have bolstered the argument that climate change is strengthening El Niño.
In a strong El Niño year, they can reach more than two degrees C above normal.

title: Cornish residents urged to "join in" with food waste drive
summary:
Understanding the benefits of recycling food waste could encourage more people to do it in future, Cornwall Council has said.
For the past two years, leftover food has been able to be taken to an anaerobic digester to be converted into methane to generate electricity and produce fertiliser.
The council said about 36,000 tonnes of food waste had been recycled to date since the introduction of its new waste service.
It said it hoped increased participation through understanding the benefits would help meet its target to recycle nearly two-thirds of Cornwall's waste by 2029.

title: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
summary:
A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods.
Across the mountains of Nepal and Tibet, climate change is causing glaciers to melt at an alarming rate.
Planet-heating emissions from burning fossil fuels such as oil, gas and coal are the primary driver of climate change.
Preliminary reports indicate that Nepal's flood warning system wasn't equipped to handle these floods.
That's despite significant government investment in flood warning systems over the last decade in Nepal.

title: What lessons can be learned from the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster?
summary:
Scientists are looking into cause and possible link to climate change.
The role of climate change in the flooding disaster in Nepal and Tibet is under scrutiny by scientists, who are trying to find out what caused the catastrophe.
Elsewhere, countries around the world have been hit by more severe weather events in recent months.
So, what lessons can be learned from Wednesday’s disaster – and others this year?

title: $5.4 billion Microsoft data center vs 41,000 petitioners — "Stopping this project is one of the most significant steps we could take"
summary:
Click for next articleOver 41,000 people have signed a petition to prevent the construction of Microsoft's hyperscale data center in Leeds, England.
In total, three data center buildings totaling around 424,000 sq ft and the required power and water infrastructure will be built.
The data center will stand on the former Skelton Grange power station site, which used to have two coal-fired power stations.
The Microsoft CEO's remarks were general and did not specifically address concerns about the future data center in Leeds.
Microsoft is working on new cooling technologies to reduce how much water data centers require.

title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 'High risk' of lake breaching and causing second flood, warns China
summary:
China has warned there is a "high risk" a lake that formed after the recent landslide near the Nepal-Tibet border may breach its banks, causing a second flood downstream.
As of Friday, an estimated 2.5 million cubic metres of water had accumulated, according to broadcaster CCTV.
Officials said that three million cubic metres of water was expected to flow into the lake between Thursday and the weekend, posing a "high risk of breach".
The barrier lake had started to overflow on Thursday.
But by Friday afternoon, state media reported that the "risk from the upstream barrier lake had come under control" and that rescue operations had resumed.

The warning comes after Wednesday's deadly flash flood in the same area which scientists say was triggered by the collapse of a mountain glacier into a river.
China correspondent Laura Bicker explains.

title: Nepal-Tibet flash floods: These two women are among nearly 300 Indians missing
summary:
The 43-year-old is now among at least 290 Indians reported missing after deadly flash floods struck along Nepal's border with Tibet.
Many of those unaccounted for were on the pilgrimage, which resumed last year after being disrupted by the pandemic and then by tensions between India and China.
Thousands of Indians have been making their way to Mount Kailash for years.

title: Watch: Blocked roads and devastation as BBC drives to site of Nepal floods
summary:
The BBC has seen widespread devastation on the way from Nepal's capital of Kathmandu to Trishuli, one of the areas worst-hit by flooding on the Tibetan border.
As well as ambulances, hearses were also seen along the route, where rescuers said entire villages had been washed away by floodwaters.
South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri reports.
